gen-fs-expose-fs-fira-sans: Tight, striking, barely pausing for breath. Fira Sans follows with generous curves at the ends of its s and a tall x-height, drawn like strips of one width.
gen-fs-expose-fs-merriweather-sans: Expose stacks its small letters nearly as high as its capitals, with hardly a pause between them. Merriweather Sans lets the page ease along, its tall, sturdy lowercase and clearly open e keeping words large and steady.
gen-fs-expose-fs-supreme:
Supreme reads crisp and dense, a heavy band of text with letters held open.

Expose adds a compressed, refined display voice above it, and that tightness against the sturdy plain sans is the pair's sharpest quality.
gen-fs-expose-general-sans: General Sans moves like one thick thread traced around smooth bends, its tall x-height filling every line. Over a long page it stays unhurried and steady, while Expose keeps the heading compressed.
gen-fs-expose-satoshi: Approachable is the first word for Satoshi, whose soaring x-height and wide-open e never look squeezed. And Expose above it, compressed and refined, makes that plain sans feel even friendlier by comparison.
gen-fs-expose-switzer: Expose packs its lowercase almost up to cap height and barely lets the letters pause between words. Switzer relaxes underneath, its wire-like sans-serif forms keeping diagonals as heavy as verticals.
gen-fs-expose-work-sans: Work Sans is modern and wiry. Its sans-serif strokes hold constant, with a high mean line, so a long passage reads smoothly beneath the tightly compressed Expose.
gen-fs-kohinoor-zerone-fs-bespoke-sans: Kohinoor Zerone draws round letters like bent wire, precise and contemporary in a display setting. Bespoke Sans is the one with room to breathe, leaving generous space between its curve ends and the stem.
gen-press-start-2p-fs-quicksand: Press Start 2P brings retro fun, with its letters pinned far apart like cut-outs. And Quicksand keeps paragraphs gentle, its round lowercase bowls and bar thickness never changing across the line.
gen-fs-nippo-fs-supreme: Supreme reads as a thick, crisp band of text. Nippo's wire-cut letters rise almost to capital height above it, and the shared single-width curves and straights tie the sans body to the display.
